title: May Election Certified: Runoffs & Charter Defeat
summary:
*   Certified the official results of the May 7 municipal election.
*   Smoot Carl-Mitchell and Charles Urdy were declared winners for City Council Places 2 and 6, respectively.
*   A runoff election was scheduled for May 28 for races where no candidate received a majority, including the Mayor's office (between Frank C. Cooksey and Lee Cooke) and Council Place 5 (between Sam Guzman and Robert Barnstone).
*   Voters rejected a proposed City Charter amendment that would have expanded the governing body to a nine-member council with district representation.

CANVASSING
Mayor Cooksey called to order the special called meeting of the Council, noting the
absence of Councilmembers Carl-Mitchell and Humphrey. Mayor Cooksey announced the purpose
of the meeting was to canvass the returns and declare the results of the May 7, 1988
General Municipal Election, and to consider calling a runoff election for Saturday, May
28, 1988.
Motion
The Council, on Mayor Pro Tem Trevino's motion, Councilmember Shipman's second, adopted a
resolution canvassing the returns and declaring the results of the May 7, 1988 General
Municipal Election.
(4-0 Vote, Councilmembers Carl-Mitchell and Humphrey absent, Councilmember Urdy out of the
room)
(See resolution attached)
Motion
The Council, on Councilmember Shipman's motion, Mayor Pro Tem Trevino's second, waived the
requirement for three readings and finally passed an ordinance calling a runoff election
for Saturday, May 28, 1988. (5-0 Vote, Councilmembers Carl-Mitchell and Humphrey absent)
